props.gloss_en: a person may not say to his fellow [on Shabbat] to hire workers for him
Rav Pappa: the 'fellow' [of the mishna] is a gentile
Rav Ashi: telling a gentile [to do it] is a shevut
a person may say to his fellow [on Shabbat]: 'will you be seen to stand with me this evening?'
the baraita's first tanna: a person may not say to his fellow 'will you be seen to stand with me this evening?'
whose is our mishna? R' Yehoshua ben Korcha's
the halakha follows R' Yehoshua ben Korcha
R' Yehoshua ben Korcha's reason is the verse 'from pursuing your affairs and speaking a word' (Isa 58:13)
speech [of one's affairs on Shabbat] is forbidden
thought [of one's affairs on Shabbat] is permitted
R' Yochanan: one may think [Torah] in every place except the bathhouse and the privy
there it is different: we require 'and your camp shall be holy' (Deut 23:15), and it is absent
that verse ('ervat davar') is needed for Rav Yehuda's [law]
a naked gentile: one may not read the Shema facing him
it goes without saying that [facing] a naked Jew it is forbidden
since it is written of them 'whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys' (Ezek 23:20)
(entertained) facing a naked gentile, one might say it is fine to read the Shema
the verse said 'and their father's nakedness they did not see' (Gen 9:23) -- [a gentile's body too is called nakedness]
Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna: calculations of a mitzva may be calculated on Shabbat
R' Elazar: one allots charity to the poor on Shabbat
R' Yochanan: one attends to saving life and to public needs on Shabbat
R' Yochanan: one goes to synagogues to attend to public affairs on Shabbat
R' Yochanan: one goes to theatres, circuses and basilicas to attend to public affairs on Shabbat
the school of Menashe: one arranges matches for children to be betrothed on Shabbat
the school of Menashe: and [one arranges] for a child, to teach him a book and to teach him a craft
your affairs are forbidden; Heaven's affairs are permitted
the verse said 'from pursuing YOUR affairs' (Isa 58:13)
Shmuel: calculations of 'what is it to you' and of 'what does it matter' may be calculated on Shabbat
the Tosefta: calculations of what has passed and of what will be are forbidden to calculate
the Tosefta: of 'what is it to you' and of 'what does it matter' it is permitted to calculate
one calculates calculations that are not needed [on Shabbat]
and one does not calculate calculations that are needed, on Shabbat
one may say to his fellow: 'so many workers I sent out on this field, so many dinars I spent on this house'
but he may not say to him: 'so much I spent, and so much I am going to spend'
this [source speaks] where the hired man's wage is [still] with him
that [source speaks] where the hired man's wage is not with him

supports.gloss_en: דתניא: לא יאמר אדם לחבירו הנראה שתעמוד עמי לערב; רבי יהושע בן קרחה אומר: אומר אדם לחבירו הנראה שתעמוד עמי לערב (bare דתניא; kind under protest)
תניא נמי הכי: חשבונות שעברו ושעתידין להיות אסור לחשבן; של מלך ושל מה בכך מותר לחשבן

objections.gloss_en: מתקיף לה רב אשי: אמירה לגוי שבות! -- telling a gentile is itself forbidden as a shevut, so on that reading too the clause is obvious; abandoned (אלא, 150a.5)
רמי ליה רב אחא בר רב הונא לרבא: מי אמר רבי יוחנן דיבור אסור הרהור מותר -- אלמא הרהור לאו כדיבור דמי? והאמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן: בכל מקום מותר להרהר חוץ מבית המרחץ ומבית הכסא!

answered_by.gloss_en: שאני התם, דבעינן והיה מחניך קדוש, וליכא (= p_shani_hatam_machanecha)

objections.gloss_en: הכא נמי כתיב ולא יראה בך ערות דבר? -- here [in the same verse] it is written 'davar' [speech], so there too only speech should be forbidden

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא מיבעי ליה לכדרב יהודה: גוי ערום אסור לקרות קריאת שמע כנגדו (= p_ervat_davar_needed)

objections.gloss_en: ודיבור מי אסיר? והא רב חסדא ורב המנונא דאמרי תרווייהו: חשבונות של מצוה מותר לחשבן בשבת; ואמר רבי אלעזר: פוסקים צדקה...; ואמר רבי יעקב בר אידי אמר רבי יוחנן: מפקחין...; ואמר רבי שמואל בר נחמני אמר רבי יוחנן: הולכין לטרטיאות...; ותנא דבי מנשה: משדכין על התינוקות...!

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר קרא ממצוא חפצך ודבר דבר -- חפציך אסורים, חפצי שמים מותרין (= p_cheftzei_shamayim_mutarin)

objections.gloss_en: ורמינהו: חושבין חשבונות שאינן צריכין... אומר אדם לחבירו כך וכך פועלים הוצאתי על שדה זו... -- the second baraita permits stating past outlays, which the Tosefta forbids

answered_by.gloss_en: ולטעמיך, קשיא לך היא גופה! אלא: הא דאיכא אגרא דאגירא גביה, הא דליכא אגרא דאגירא גביה (= p_okimta_ika_agra, p_okimta_leika_agra; the mapping of the two הא is Steinsaltz's)
